name: Open Items
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · USD · Subsequent events and going concern workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion expressed

Corliss Medical Group settled the disputed final billing on October 8, 2026: $110,000.00 by October 30, 2026 against $186,935.00 billed. The dispute existed at June 30, so the settlement is evidence of the June 30 amount (a recognized event, AU-C 560). Proposed: reduce the receivable by $76,935.00 at June 30, against revenue or bad debt expense as the CPA decides. This settles the receivables testing’s AR-03.

Brindlewood School District denied HCS’s time extension on September 15, 2026; the $41,250.00 of liquidated damages for late completion before June 30 is final. Proposed: reduce contract revenue and the retainage receivable at June 30. This settles AR-02.

The draft subsequent events note gives only the October 9 advance. It must also disclose the $1,200,000.00 advance of August 14, 2026, the $150,000.00 dividend, the bank’s commitment to renew the line to March 31, 2029 with its covenant relief, and the Tideflats estimate revision of $1,196,000.00 after August’s events (WIP-02), and state the date through which events were evaluated, October 22, 2026 (ASC 855).

Conditions raised substantial doubt: the $3,500,000.00 line matures March 31, 2027 and, without its renewal, cash falls to ($2,089,899.67) in March 2027. The bank’s binding commitment, accepted October 20, 2026, and the board’s suspension of dividends alleviate it. The draft note says there were no such conditions; ASC 205-40 requires it to describe the conditions, management’s evaluation and the plans. Proposed wording is in the Going Concern tab. With the doubt alleviated, AU-C 570 calls for no going concern section in the report. The CPA concludes.

September 30 tangible net worth is $6,629,999.00 as the interim books show it and $6,217,264.00 without PCO-14, with September interest and with SE-01 and SE-02: $282,736.00 below the loan agreement’s minimum, $217,264.00 above the commitment’s relieved $6,000,000.00. The CPA confirms with the bank that the relief applies before dating the report; the plans rest on it.

The forecast collects the Corliss billing in full in October; the settlement pays $110,000.00. Corrected, the lowest month-end cash is $1,333,165.33; without PCO-14 as well, $693,165.33. Management updates the forecast.

Recognized events the other FY2026 areas already proposed, confirmed here by what happened after June 30: WIP-01 $103,600.00, AR-01 $28,600.00, UL-04 $28,665.00, UL-01 $186,400.00 (with its revenue effect, CROSS-01) and UL-02 $23,480.00. The CPA records them with those areas’ findings.
Materiality is proposed at $340,000.00, 0.5% of revenue, with performance materiality $255,000.00. The engagement partner sets the final amounts.
The representation letter must be dated as of the report date, October 22, 2026, and cover subsequent events and management’s plans and their feasibility (AU-C 580 and AU-C 570).
This review runs to October 21, 2026. The CPA updates the inquiries, the minutes and the cash to the report date and dates the report no earlier than the evidence.
These are draft workpapers and a draft findings memo for the engagement partner. They are not an audit report and give no opinion. Nothing has been signed, posted or sent.
